results.term_definition: A comet nucleus is the core of a comet. This is a solid object, similar to a dirty snowball, made with ice and rocky, dusty particles. Far from the Sun the nucleus is the sole component of the comet. Closer to the Sun a comet's nucleus is heated due to sunlight. This causes the surface ice to sublimate. The sublimated ice and the dust embedded in it are ejected and surround the nucleus as a coma with a tail pointing away from the Sun.
